text:
matt: quick heads up — we saw a latency tail starting ~18:12 on pool-A when bursts hit long-context chat sessions, spikes up to +180ms. KV eviction rate jumped at the same time. opening thread to capture notes

anita: saw that too, noticed FIFO evict count doubled vs normal. diff looks correlated with last night's LRU->hybrid change? :thinking:

matt: hmm we merged the small change to eviction heuristics (commit abc123) last night. is the hybrid mode falling back to FIFO under memory pressure?

cheng: attaching quick metric dump: `kv_evicted: 1220`, `kv_reuse_hits: 84`, `kv_frag_pct: 27.3` over 5m window. page_faults per sec also jumped.

nora: stack traces from the slow requests look like latency is dominated by `kv_page_in` and `slab_compact` steps, not model kernels. suspecting thrash between evict and immediate reinserts.

matt: can someone produce a tiny repro? I ran a scripted workload hitting 100 concurrent long contexts and saw the same tail. command I used: `wrk -t8 -c100 -d120s --script long_context.lua http://pool-a/api/generate`

cheng: repro confirmed locally — odd thing: when switching the eviction policy flag to force pure-LRU, the reuse_hits rose and latencies improved ~40ms p50. when forcing FIFO latencies got worse.

anita: that suggests correctness/regression in hybrid fallback path. maybe our LRU timestamp bump isn't atomic and reinserts race with eviction.

perf-bot: pprof report uploaded: /tmp/pprof-kv-2276543210.svg (hot: kv_page_in, slab_lock_wait, memmove) :eyes:

nora: looking at logs: several entries like `evict: removed key K@slot=0x7f, reinserting key K@slot=0x9f` within 2ms. sounds like reinsert-after-evict race; we might be double-counting active entries leading to fragmentation.

matt: could explain memory growth in long contexts — evict removes pointer but reinsert creates new chunk -> fragmentation and extra page-ins.

cheng: quick patch idea: make reinsert fast-path check for concurrent eviction and reuse the freed slot instead of allocating. I'll try a small prototype in a branch and run the same wrk test.

anita: also add histograms for `evict_latency_ms` and `reinsert_latency_ms` and per-slab free-list depth. we lack visibility there.

matt: agree. action items: (1) cheng to prototype in a branch and run stress (2) nora to add extra metrics/dashboards and enable on pool-A for 1h (3) anita to prepare canary rollback plan for commit abc123 if repro strong.

cheng: pushed branch `kv-reuse-slot-fastpath` and ran 2 x 2m wrk runs. results: p95 reduced from 310ms->250ms and reuse_hits +70%. pushing canary to pool-B for validation.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started — pool-B nodes: node-12,node-13. sha: kv-reuse-slot-fastpath

nora: enabling extra metrics on pool-A now, will snapshot after 15m.

anita: if canary looks good, prefer fixing the hybrid fallback atomically rather than full revert. we should still be ready to roll back.

matt: thanks team. please drop short notes here with canary outcome. I'll create a follow-up ticket with logs and perf graphs. :thumbsup:

cheng: quick update 15m later — pool-B canary looks stable, no eviction spikes under the same wrk script. tagging graphs: `canary_vs_prod_evictions.png`.

nora: pool-A metrics after 15m show evict_count steady and fragmentation trending down on canary. but prod still noisy — need rollout plan.

matt: great. we'll do staged rollout once we have runbook and alerts adjusted. leaving thread open for post-rollout postmortem.

anita: filed runbook PR and added alert `kv_eviction_rate > 500/m` to paged channel. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/kv/PR/542

matt: closing loop — follow-up ticket: INF-1178 with links to branch, pprof, wrk scripts, and graphs. thanks everyone.
